<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Phase 1 of #61396. Design comments belong in the RFC.

This PR gives the offloading manager the cause of each store, and moves the connector's store code into one handler per trigger. It adds `ON_HANDOFF` for state blocks that the KV cache manager hands off. The next PR adds `ON_OVERWRITE`, lets the manager select its triggers, and adds the `lazy` store mode.

This PR replaces #61426.

## Claims

- New `StoreTrigger` enum with `ON_COMPUTE` (the chunks are complete) and `ON_HANDOFF` (a state block is about to be reused, so the store cannot be postponed).
- `prepare_store` and `complete_store` take a required keyword-only `trigger`. `complete_store` also takes `success` keyword-only. An out-of-tree manager must add both parameters.
- The connector makes store jobs through a `StoreTriggerHandler` per trigger, in `offloading/store_triggers/`. Handlers offer keys and jobs through `StoreJobSink`. The scheduler owns the job ID, status, trigger stamp, fences, flushes and completion.
- Handlers are isolated: no handler knows of another, and each keeps its own state. The scheduler keeps global state and gives every handler the same hooks (`on_load_scheduled`, `on_request_removed`, `on_request_restarted`, `reset`, `first_live_chunk_idx`, `build_store_jobs`).
- `first_live_chunk_idx` returns the first chunk of a group whose GPU block ids a handler may still read, or `None` when it reads none. The scheduler zeroes stale sliding-window block ids only from the lowest value on.
- The scheduler adds `OnHandoffStoreHandler` whenever the config has a copy-on-write source group (`MambaSpec` with `mamba_cache_mode="align"`), before the manager's triggers. The job-ID order does not change, and the manager can decline these stores in `prepare_store`.
- The tiering manager gives the trigger to its primary tier. A promotion is not a store, so `prepare_write` and `complete_write` are real methods.

## Validation

- Each of the 11 commits passes `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector` and `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py`.
- At the tip, `tests/v1/kv_offload` plus `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector` gives 1586 passed, 13 skipped, 11 failed. All 11 failures are `FileNotFoundError` on `/dev/shm`, which macOS does not have (`test_cache_reset*` and tiering p2p). `test_shared_offload_region.py` and `test_gpu_worker.py` are deselected for the same reason. These tests fail the same way on unmodified `main`.
- `pre-commit run` passes, including mypy.
- Rebased onto `main` `5c97556318` on 2026-11-04. Two new upstream behaviors are absorbed: lookahead block hashes suppress the EAGLE tail drop (`apply_eagle_drop`), and a store spec keeps null pages inside a chunk as placeholders.
- End-to-end sanity, one H100 per model, 0 server errors, 0 preemptions. Head `29f69746b0`; Qwen base `5c97556318`:

| model | workload | side | req/s | mean TTFT ms | TPOT ms | store GB | load GB | hits |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-8B | client.py 32x3188, 3 rounds | head | - | - | - | 30.09 | 15.01 | 99.8% (R3) |
| Qwen3-8B | client.py | base | - | - | - | 30.09 | 15.01 | 99.8% (R3) |
| Qwen3-8B | prefix_repetition 48x4096 | head | 30.72 | 574.9 | 16.71 | 43.51 | 295.97 | 87% |
| Qwen3-8B | prefix_repetition | base | 31.04 | 570.6 | 16.40 | 43.51 | 295.37 | 87% |
| Falcon-H1-0.5B (align) | client.py 32x3332, 3 rounds | head | - | - | - | 4.71 | 2.35 | 96.0% (R3) |
| Falcon-H1-0.5B (align) | prefix_repetition 32x4096 | head | 22.21 | 334.7 | 14.62 | 2.82 | 18.80 | 82% |

- The Qwen client counters are identical on both sides: 30.088 GB stored, 15.007 GB loaded, 101776 hits on 306541 queries.
- Falcon handlers are `['ON_HANDOFF', 'ON_COMPUTE']`, with CoW source group 1 (`MambaSpec`). A measurement-only wrapper counted 341 offers, 96 keys and 96 jobs under `ON_HANDOFF`; `ON_COMPUTE` took 123 offers, 416 keys and 112 jobs. The CPU tier grew by 4.71 GB. `ON_COMPUTE` skips `requires_cow_source` groups, so the Mamba state can reach the CPU tier only through the handoff path.
- Caveat: greedy text is not bit-stable after a CPU restore. On 2026-11-04 the Falcon head matched 24 of 32 rounds, and a no-offload control matched 32 of 32. The 2026-11-01 run of the same workload matched 29 of 32 on head and 30 of 32 on base `68473496ee`, with byte-identical offload counters (4.7056 GB store, 2.3528 GB load, 102400/320291 hits). The drift is pre-existing in the Mamba-align CPU-restore path, is not from this PR, and I have not root-caused it. Qwen on 2026-11-04: 28 of 32 on head against 29 of 32 on base, the same class as the 2026-10-21 run.

CI runs these tests in `v1/kv_offload` and `v1/kv_connector/unit`. The KV-Offload lm-eval jobs also trigger on these paths.

## Compatibility

`prepare_store(keys, req_context, *, trigger)` and `complete_store(keys, req_context, *, trigger, success)` break out-of-tree managers. That is the only break. There is no user-visible config change.

Eager behavior is unchanged. The aligned-boundary and partial-tail stores keep the same source, the same keys and the same job-ID order. They now live in `OnHandoffStoreHandler`.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to write the code, the tests and this text. I reviewed each changed line and can explain each design choice.

---

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.

- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.

</details>

nodes.body:
This will be useful for lazy offloading as well.
Claude suggests we put them in their own handler:

**Where should the hand-off stores live?**

`OnComputeStoreHandler` holds two store kinds that are not `ON_COMPUTE` stores: the aligned boundary stores and the partial-tail CoW stores, both fed by `kv_connector_block_state.boundary_state_offloads`. They differ from chunk stores in three ways:

- **Who decides when.** The KV cache manager sends the hand-off when the recurrent state block is about to be reused. Neither the eager nor the lazy policy picks that moment.
- **The source is short-lived.** The CoW copy is offered once, so the store can't be postponed. Lazy mode must store it at the same step as eager mode.
- **No per-request progress.** It never reads `_next_stored_chunk_idxs`; it works from `req_status` and the hand-off only.

So every store mode stores these the same way, at the same time. That makes it a trigger of its own, not part of `ON_COMPUTE`. If it stays in `OnComputeStoreHandler`, a manager that later selects only `ON_OVERWRITE` or lazy silently stops storing Mamba `align` state. Hybrid models then get no prefix hits from offload, and nothing in the logs says why.

Suggested layout:

```
store_triggers/
  base.py        StoreTriggerHandler
  on_compute.py  OnComputeStoreHandler   (chunk stores only)
  handoff.py     HandoffStoreHandler     (aligned boundary + partial tail, _cow_source_groups)
  candidates.py  select_store_candidates (was common.py; avoids two `common` modules)
```

- Add `StoreTrigger.ON_HANDOFF`, so the manager sees the real cause. A lazy manager can then admit these stores without running its overwrite admission.
- The scheduler adds this handler on its own whenever the config can produce hand-offs (`supports_partial_tail` or any `requires_cow_source` group). The manager doesn't select it. A manager can still decline these stores in `prepare_store`.
- Run it before `OnComputeStoreHandler`. That keeps today's job-ID order, so this stays a pure move.
- It also retires the name `_build_partial_tail_store_jobs`, which today also runs the aligned-boundary path.

detail.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Phase 1 of #61396. Design comments belong in the RFC.

This PR gives the offloading manager the cause of each store, and moves the connector's store code into one handler per trigger. It adds `ON_HANDOFF` for state blocks that the KV cache manager hands off. The next PR adds `ON_OVERWRITE`, lets the manager select its triggers, and adds the `lazy` store mode.

This PR replaces #61426.

## Claims

- New `StoreTrigger` enum with `ON_COMPUTE` (the chunks are complete) and `ON_HANDOFF` (a state block is about to be reused, so the store cannot be postponed).
- `prepare_store` and `complete_store` take a required keyword-only `trigger`. `complete_store` also takes `success` keyword-only. An out-of-tree manager must add both parameters.
- The connector makes store jobs through a `StoreTriggerHandler` per trigger, in `offloading/store_triggers/`. Handlers offer keys and jobs through `StoreJobSink`. The scheduler owns the job ID, status, trigger stamp, fences, flushes and completion.
- Handlers are isolated: no handler knows of another, and each keeps its own state. The scheduler keeps global state and gives every handler the same hooks (`on_load_scheduled`, `on_request_removed`, `on_request_restarted`, `reset`, `first_live_chunk_idx`, `build_store_jobs`).
- `first_live_chunk_idx` returns the first chunk of a group whose GPU block ids a handler may still read, or `None` when it reads none. The scheduler zeroes stale sliding-window block ids only from the lowest value on.
- The scheduler adds `OnHandoffStoreHandler` whenever the config has a copy-on-write source group (`MambaSpec` with `mamba_cache_mode="align"`), before the manager's triggers. The job-ID order does not change, and the manager can decline these stores in `prepare_store`.
- The tiering manager gives the trigger to its primary tier. A promotion is not a store, so `prepare_write` and `complete_write` are real methods.

## Validation

- Each of the 11 commits passes `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector` and `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py`.
- At the tip, `tests/v1/kv_offload` plus `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector` gives 1586 passed, 13 skipped, 11 failed. All 11 failures are `FileNotFoundError` on `/dev/shm`, which macOS does not have (`test_cache_reset*` and tiering p2p). `test_shared_offload_region.py` and `test_gpu_worker.py` are deselected for the same reason. These tests fail the same way on unmodified `main`.
- `pre-commit run` passes, including mypy.
- Rebased onto `main` `5c97556318` on 2026-11-04. Two new upstream behaviors are absorbed: lookahead block hashes suppress the EAGLE tail drop (`apply_eagle_drop`), and a store spec keeps null pages inside a chunk as placeholders.
- End-to-end sanity, one H100 per model, 0 server errors, 0 preemptions. Head `29f69746b0`; Qwen base `5c97556318`:

| model | workload | side | req/s | mean TTFT ms | TPOT ms | store GB | load GB | hits |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-8B | client.py 32x3188, 3 rounds | head | - | - | - | 30.09 | 15.01 | 99.8% (R3) |
| Qwen3-8B | client.py | base | - | - | - | 30.09 | 15.01 | 99.8% (R3) |
| Qwen3-8B | prefix_repetition 48x4096 | head | 30.72 | 574.9 | 16.71 | 43.51 | 295.97 | 87% |
| Qwen3-8B | prefix_repetition | base | 31.04 | 570.6 | 16.40 | 43.51 | 295.37 | 87% |
| Falcon-H1-0.5B (align) | client.py 32x3332, 3 rounds | head | - | - | - | 4.71 | 2.35 | 96.0% (R3) |
| Falcon-H1-0.5B (align) | prefix_repetition 32x4096 | head | 22.21 | 334.7 | 14.62 | 2.82 | 18.80 | 82% |

- The Qwen client counters are identical on both sides: 30.088 GB stored, 15.007 GB loaded, 101776 hits on 306541 queries.
- Falcon handlers are `['ON_HANDOFF', 'ON_COMPUTE']`, with CoW source group 1 (`MambaSpec`). A measurement-only wrapper counted 341 offers, 96 keys and 96 jobs under `ON_HANDOFF`; `ON_COMPUTE` took 123 offers, 416 keys and 112 jobs. The CPU tier grew by 4.71 GB. `ON_COMPUTE` skips `requires_cow_source` groups, so the Mamba state can reach the CPU tier only through the handoff path.
- Caveat: greedy text is not bit-stable after a CPU restore. On 2026-11-04 the Falcon head matched 24 of 32 rounds, and a no-offload control matched 32 of 32. The 2026-11-01 run of the same workload matched 29 of 32 on head and 30 of 32 on base `68473496ee`, with byte-identical offload counters (4.7056 GB store, 2.3528 GB load, 102400/320291 hits). The drift is pre-existing in the Mamba-align CPU-restore path, is not from this PR, and I have not root-caused it. Qwen on 2026-11-04: 28 of 32 on head against 29 of 32 on base, the same class as the 2026-10-21 run.

CI runs these tests in `v1/kv_offload` and `v1/kv_connector/unit`. The KV-Offload lm-eval jobs also trigger on these paths.

## Compatibility

`prepare_store(keys, req_context, *, trigger)` and `complete_store(keys, req_context, *, trigger, success)` break out-of-tree managers. That is the only break. There is no user-visible config change.

Eager behavior is unchanged. The aligned-boundary and partial-tail stores keep the same source, the same keys and the same job-ID order. They now live in `OnHandoffStoreHandler`.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to write the code, the tests and this text. I reviewed each changed line and can explain each design choice.

+def test_stores_pass_the_trigger_to_prepare_and_complete(request_runner):
+    """The scheduler gives a store job's trigger to both prepare_store and
+    complete_store."""
+    tokens_per_block = 4
+    blocks_per_chunk = 3
+    runner = request_runner(
+        blocks_per_chunk=blocks_per_chunk,
+        block_size=tokens_per_block,
+        num_gpu_blocks=100,
+        async_scheduling=False,
+    )
+    runner.new_request(token_ids=[0] * tokens_per_block * blocks_per_chunk)
+    prepared: list[StoreTrigger] = []
+    completed: list[StoreTrigger] = []
+
+    def prepare_store(keys, req_context, trigger):
+        prepared.append(trigger)
+        return generate_store_output(keys)
+
+    def complete_store(keys, req_context, *, trigger, success=True):
+        completed.append(trigger)
+
+    runner.manager.prepare_store.side_effect = prepare_store
+    runner.manager.complete_store.side_effect = complete_store
+
+    runner.run(decoded_tokens=[0, 0], expected_stored=(0, 1, 2))
+    runner.run(decoded_tokens=[EOS_TOKEN_ID])
+
+    assert prepared and set(prepared) == {StoreTrigger.ON_COMPUTE}
+    assert completed == [StoreTrigger.ON_COMPUTE]
+
+
+class _RecordingStoreHandler(OnComputeStoreHandler):
+    """An ON_COMPUTE handler that records the hooks the scheduler calls."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *args: Any):
+        super().__init__(*args)
+        self.removed: list[str] = []
+
+    def on_request_removed(self, req_id):
+        self.removed.append(req_id)
+        super().on_request_removed(req_id)
+
+
+def _install_recording_handler(runner) -> _RecordingStoreHandler:
+    sched = runner.connector_scheduler
+    handler = _RecordingStoreHandler(sched.config, sched._events_tracker)
+    sched._store_handlers[StoreTrigger.ON_COMPUTE] = handler
+    return handler
+
+
+def test_store_handler_hears_each_request_removal(request_runner):
+    """Each path that removes a request tells the handler, so a handler can
+    drop its own state of the request."""
+    block_size = 4
+    blocks_per_chunk = 3
+    tokens_per_chunk = block_size * blocks_per_chunk
+    runner = request_runner(
+        blocks_per_chunk=blocks_per_chunk,
+        block_size=block_size,
+        num_gpu_blocks=100,
+        async_scheduling=False,
+    )
+    handler = _install_recording_handler(runner)
+    sched = runner.connector_scheduler
+
+    # Finished with no store job.
+    runner.manager.prepare_store.side_effect = lambda keys, req_context, trigger: (
+        generate_store_output([])
+    )
+    runner.new_request(token_ids=[1] * tokens_per_chunk)
+    runner.run(decoded_tokens=[EOS_TOKEN_ID])
+    assert handler.removed == [str(runner.req_id)]
+
+    # Finished, then the last store job completes.
+    runner.manager.prepare_store.side_effect = lambda keys, req_context, trigger: (
+        generate_store_output(keys)
+    )
+    runner.new_request(token_ids=[2] * tokens_per_chunk)
+    runner.run(decoded_tokens=[EOS_TOKEN_ID], expected_stored=(0, 1, 2))
+    assert handler.removed[1:] == [str(runner.req_id)]
+
+    # Finished with a store job in flight, then a cache reset.
+    runner.new_request(token_ids=[3] * tokens_per_chunk)
+    runner.run(decoded_tokens=[EOS_TOKEN_ID], complete_transfers=False)
+    store_statuses = [s for s in sched._job_statuses.values() if s.is_store]
+    assert store_statuses
+    assert all(s.trigger is StoreTrigger.ON_COMPUTE for s in store_statuses)
+    assert handler.removed[2:] == []
+    sched.reset_cache()
+    assert handler.removed[2:] == [str(runner.req_id)]
+
+

+class GroupOffloadConfig(NamedTuple):
+    group_idx: int
+    tokens_per_block: int
+    tokens_per_chunk: int
+    hashes_per_chunk: int
+    # KV cache spec metadata propagated onto emitted BlockStored events so
+    # KV-aware consumers can classify and filter the group.
+    kv_event_group_spec: OffloadingEventGroupSpec
+    # None below means full attention
+    sliding_window_size_in_chunks: int | None
+    kv_cache_spec: KVCacheSpec
+    # Cached manager class for this group's KV cache spec, resolved at init time
+    manager_cls: type[SingleTypeKVCacheManager]
+    # Partial-tail data for this group comes from the scheduler's CoW hand-off
+    # rather than the request block table.
+    requires_cow_source: bool = False
+    # True for EAGLE/MTP draft-model attention groups. Connectors using legacy
+    # hashes exclude their trailing chunk from store and load scheduling.
+    is_eagle_group: bool = False
+
+    def load_window_size_in_chunks(self, num_tokens: int) -> int | None:
+        window = self.sliding_window_size_in_chunks
+        if isinstance(self.kv_cache_spec, SlidingWindowSpec):
+            assert window is not None
+            # Lookup rounds the right edge up, but allocation retains the
+            # window ending at the actual hit boundary, possibly one chunk left.
+            right_padding = -num_tokens % self.tokens_per_chunk
+            window = max(
+                window,
+                cdiv(
+                    self.kv_cache_spec.sliding_window
+                    - 1
+                    + self.kv_cache_spec.extra_retained_tokens
+                    + right_padding,
+                    self.tokens_per_chunk,
+                ),
+            )
+        return window
+

+def resolve_mamba_align_size(
+    spec: "OffloadingSpec", kv_cache_config: KVCacheConfig
+) -> int | None:
+    """Scan all KV cache groups in *spec* and return the single mamba alignment
+    size, or None if no group requires mamba alignment.
+
+    For MambaSpec groups in "align" cache mode the hit window must be
+    rounded down to a multiple of the offloaded chunk size. Asserts that all
+    such groups agree on the same value.
+    """
+    mamba_align_size: int | None = None
+    for group in spec.config.groups:
+        tokens_per_block = group.tokens_per_block
+        kv_spec = kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[group.group_id].kv_cache_spec
+        if isinstance(kv_spec, MambaSpec) and kv_spec.mamba_cache_mode == "align":
+            tokens_per_chunk = tokens_per_block * spec.blocks_per_chunk
+            assert mamba_align_size is None or mamba_align_size == tokens_per_chunk
+            mamba_align_size = tokens_per_chunk
+    return mamba_align_size

+            ),
+            kv_bytes_per_token=sum(
+                _group_kv_bytes_per_block(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[g.group_id])
+                // g.tokens_per_block
+                for g in spec.config.groups
+            ),
+            eagle_proof_margins=eagle_proof_margins,
+            num_hash_lookahead_tokens=vllm_config.num_hash_lookahead_tokens,
+        )
+
+
+@dataclass
+class RequestGroupState:
+    offload_keys: list[OffloadKey] = field(default_factory=list)
+    block_ids: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)
+    # Number of offloaded chunks hit (including GPU prefix cache)
+    # when the request first started
+    num_hit_chunks: int = 0
+    # End (exclusive) of the chunks that the current complete-chunk lookup
+    # confirmed as ready hits, including a popped EAGLE chunk.
+    lookup_hit_end_chunk_idx: int = 0
+
+
+@dataclass(slots=True)
+class RequestOffloadState:
+    config: SchedulerOffloadConfig
+    req: Request
+    req_context: ReqContext
+    offloading_context: RequestOffloadingContext
+    group_states: tuple[RequestGroupState, ...] = field(init=False)
+    # upper bound on tokens to load for this request; None means no cap
+    max_load_tokens: int | None = None
+    # upper bound on tokens to offload for this request; None means no cap
+    max_offload_tokens: int | None = None
+    # number of hits in the GPU cache
+    num_locally_computed_tokens: int = 0
+    # In-flight job IDs. Per the connector's invariant, at any given time
+    # this contains either a single load job, or one or more store jobs.
+    transfer_jobs: set[int] = field(default_factory=set)
+    # time.monotonic() of this request's first deferred offload lookup;
+    # None once consumed (observed) or while no lookup is pending.
+    deferred_lookup_start_time: float | None = None
+    # Fine-grained token boundary selected beyond the last complete offload
+    # chunk. It is consumed when the corresponding load is scheduled.
+    partial_tail_boundary: int | None = None
+    # True once a load from the offload tier was scheduled for this request.
+    loaded_from_offload: bool = False
+    # Loaded attention keys cover their token positions. Recurrent state
+    # supports the whole reused external prefix.
+    load_key_ranges: list[tuple[int, int, OffloadKey]] = field(default_factory=list)
+    # True once on_request_finished has been signaled to the manager.
+    finished_signaled: bool = False
+    # A load for this request failed; all its later lookups, including after
+    # preemption, skip the offloaded cache so a faulting load is not retried.
+    load_failed: bool = False
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        self.group_states = tuple(
+            RequestGroupState() for _ in self.config.kv_group_configs
+        )
+        params = self.req.kv_transfer_params
+
+        # NOTE: This field is experimental and subject to change in the future.
+        raw = params.get("max_load_tokens") if params else None
+        if type(raw) is int and raw >= 0:
+            self.max_load_tokens = raw
+            logger.debug(
+                "Request %s: max_load_tokens set to %d",
+                self.req.request_id,
+                raw,
+            )
+        elif raw is not None:
+            logger.warning(
+                "max_load_tokens must be a non-negative int, got %r; ignoring", raw
+            )
+
+        # NOTE: This field is experimental and subject to change in the future.
+        raw = params.get("max_offload_tokens") if params else None
+        if type(raw) is int and raw >= 0:
+            self.max_offload_tokens = raw
+            logger.debug(
+                "Request %s: max_offload_tokens set to %d",
+                self.req.request_id,
+                raw,
+            )
+        elif raw is not None:
+            logger.warning(
+                "max_offload_tokens must be a non-negative int, got %r; ignoring", raw
+            )
+
+    def update_offload_keys(self) -> None:
+        for group_config, group_state in zip(
+            self.config.kv_group_configs, self.group_states
+        ):
+            stride = group_config.hashes_per_chunk
+            start = stride * (len(group_state.offload_keys) + 1) - 1
+            for req_block_hash in self.req.block_hashes[start::stride]:
+                key = make_offload_key(req_block_hash, group_config.group_idx)
+                group_state.offload_keys.append(key)
+                self.req_context.set_offload_key_position(
+                    key,
+                    len(group_state.offload_keys) * group_config.tokens_per_chunk,
+                )
+
+    def update_block_id_groups(
+        self, new_block_id_groups: tuple[list[int], ...] | None
+    ) -> None:
+        if new_block_id_groups is None:
+            return
+
+        for group_config, group_state in zip(
+            self.config.kv_group_configs, self.group_states
+        ):
+            group_state.block_ids.extend(new_block_id_groups[group_config.group_idx])
+
+    def storable_chunks(
+        self,
+        group_config: "GroupOffloadConfig",
+        group_state: RequestGroupState,
+        num_offloadable_tokens: int,
+        apply_eagle_drop: bool,
+    ) -> int:
+        """Number of allocated and keyed leading chunks eligible for store.
+
+        With legacy hashes, the volatile trailing chunk of an EAGLE/MTP group
+        is excluded while decoding: the draft-layer KV of the last accepted
+        position may be rewritten after spec-token rejection. During prefill
+        the trailing chunk is stable (the draft input for a chunk's last
+        position is the next prompt token), so it is stored immediately.
+        Once the request has finished, no further spec-token rejection can
+        rewrite the tail, so the exclusion is lifted and the final chunk
+        becomes storable (issue #52735). The exclusion must be applied
+        consistently everywhere the ON_COMPUTE progress is derived:
+        otherwise the trailing chunk of each step is skipped on collection but
+        jumped over by the progress, so it is never re-considered
+        and a permanent hole breaks prefix-reuse lookup. ``is_finished`` is
+        monotonic, so the finish-time calls all see the lifted exclusion.
+        """
+        num_chunks = num_offloadable_tokens // group_config.tokens_per_chunk
+        is_decoding = num_offloadable_tokens > self.req.num_prompt_tokens
+        # Finished requests have no pending speculation.
+        if (
+            apply_eagle_drop
+            and group_config.is_eagle_group
+            and is_decoding
+            and not self.req.is_finished()
+        ):
+            num_chunks = max(0, num_chunks - 1)
+        num_allocated_chunks = (
+            len(group_state.block_ids) // self.config.blocks_per_chunk
+        )
+        num_keyed_chunks = len(group_state.offload_keys)
+        return min(num_chunks, num_allocated_chunks, num_keyed_chunks)
+
+    def num_offloadable_tokens(self, num_computed_tokens: int) -> int:
+        num = min(num_computed_tokens, self.req.num_tokens)
+        if self.config.num_hash_lookahead_tokens:
+            num = min(
+                num,
+                len(self.req.block_hashes) * self.config.tokens_per_hash,
+            )
+        if self.max_offload_tokens is not None:
+            num = min(num, self.max_offload_tokens)
+        if self.config.offload_prompt_only:
+            num = min(num, self.req.num_prompt_tokens)
+        return num
+
+    def register_boundary_key(self, group_idx: int, boundary_tokens: int) -> OffloadKey:
+        hash_idx = boundary_tokens // self.config.tokens_per_hash - 1
+        key = make_offload_key(self.req.block_hashes[hash_idx], group_idx)
+        self.req_context.set_offload_key_position(key, boundary_tokens)
+        return key
+
+    def update_num_hit_chunks(self, num_cached_tokens: int) -> None:
+        for group_config, group_state in zip(
+            self.config.kv_group_configs, self.group_states
+        ):
+            group_state.num_hit_chunks = (
+                num_cached_tokens // group_config.tokens_per_chunk
+            )

+class StoreJobSink(Protocol):
+    """The scheduler's store-job intake for one handler, in one step.
+
+    The sink carries the trigger of its handler, so a handler cannot stamp a
+    job with the wrong cause. The scheduler gives each job its ID and tracks
+    it.
+    """
+
+    def prepare_store(
+        self, keys: Collection[OffloadKey], req_context: ReqContext
+    ) -> PrepareStoreOutput | None:
+        """Offer keys to the manager, with the trigger of this handler."""
+        ...
+
+    def add_job(
+        self,
+        req_id: ReqId,
+        keys: Collection[OffloadKey],
+        src_spec: GPULoadStoreSpec,
+        dst_spec: LoadStoreSpec,
+        *,
+        fenced_block_ids: list[int] | None = None,
+        deferred_fence_block_ids: list[int] | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Make a store job, and let the scheduler track it."""
+        ...
+
+
+class StoreTriggerHandler(ABC):
+    """Makes the store jobs of one StoreTrigger.
+
+    The handler offers chunks to the manager through the sink, and describes
+    the store jobs. The scheduler gives the jobs their IDs, tracks them, and
+    completes them.
+
+    Handlers are isolated. A handler does not know of other handlers, and its
+    result does not depend on which handlers run, or on their order. A handler
+    keeps its own state. The scheduler holds only global state, and gives the
+    same hooks to each handler.
+    """
+
+    # The trigger that this handler serves.
+    trigger: ClassVar[StoreTrigger]
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: SchedulerOffloadConfig,
+        events_tracker: OffloadingEventsTracker,
+    ):
+        self._config = config
+        self._events_tracker = events_tracker
+
+    def on_load_scheduled(
+        self,
+        req_status: RequestOffloadState,
+        num_cached_tokens: int,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Called when the scheduler makes a load job for a request.
+
+        Args:
+            req_status: the request of the load.
+            num_cached_tokens: the number of tokens on the GPU after the load.
+
+        """
+        return
+
+    def on_request_removed(self, req_id: ReqId) -> None:
+        """Called after the scheduler removes the state of a request.
+
+        Args:
+            req_id: the removed request.
+
+        """
+        return
+
+    def on_request_restarted(self, req_id: ReqId) -> None:
+        """Called when a request starts again from token 0, for example after
+        a preemption. Its GPU blocks are gone.
+
+        Args:
+            req_id: the restarted request.
+
+        """
+        return
+
+    def reset(self) -> None:
+        """Called when the scheduler resets the cache, after it clears the jobs."""
+        return
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def first_live_chunk_idx(
+        self, req_status: RequestOffloadState, config_idx: int
+    ) -> int | None:
+        """The first chunk of a group whose GPU block ids this handler may
+        still read.
+
+        The scheduler zeroes stale sliding-window block ids only from the
+        lowest of these chunks on.
+
+        Args:
+            req_status: the request that holds the group.
+            config_idx: the index of the group in the offloading config.
+
+        Returns:
+            The first live chunk, or None if this handler reads no chunks of
+            the request.
+
+        """
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def build_store_jobs(
+        self,
+        scheduler_output: SchedulerOutput,
+        req_states: Mapping[ReqId, RequestOffloadState],
+        sink: StoreJobSink,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Offer the chunks of this trigger to the manager, and make the jobs.
+
+        Args:
+            scheduler_output: the output of the current scheduler step.
+            req_states: the state of each tracked request.
+            sink: the intake for the store jobs of this step.
+
+        """

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+from dataclasses import replace
+from typing import NamedTuple
+
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.offloading.state import (
+    GroupOffloadConfig,
+    RequestOffloadState,
+    SchedulerOffloadConfig,
+)
+from vllm.v1.core.sched.output import SchedulerOutput
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import SlidingWindowSpec
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.base import OffloadKey
+from vllm.v1.request import RequestStatus
+
+
+class StoreCandidates(NamedTuple):
+    """The computed chunks of a request that a trigger can store."""
+
+    num_offloadable_tokens: int
+    keys: list[OffloadKey]
+    # (start_chunk_idx, end_chunk_idx) of each group
+    group_ranges: list[tuple[int, int]]
+
+
+def select_store_candidates(
+    config: SchedulerOffloadConfig,
+    scheduler_output: SchedulerOutput,
+    req_status: RequestOffloadState,
+    start_chunk_idxs: Sequence[int],
+) -> StoreCandidates:
+    """Select the computed chunks of a request, from the given chunk of each group.
+
+    Args:
+        config: the scheduler offloading config.
+        scheduler_output: the output of the current scheduler step.
+        req_status: the request.
+        start_chunk_idxs: for each group, the first chunk that the trigger did
+            not store yet.
+
+    Returns:
+        The keys and positions of the reachable chunks, and the chunk range of
+        each group.
+
+    """
+    blocks_per_chunk = config.blocks_per_chunk
+    req = req_status.req
+
+    if req.status is RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED:
+        num_tokens_after_batch = req.num_computed_tokens
+    elif req.is_finished():
+        # Clamp to the GPU prefix cache's commit point. The final sampled
+        # token's slot is never committed (under spec decode it holds a
+        # rejected draft's KV), so a block ending there must not be stored.
+        # A request that finished before its prefill completed (e.g. an
+        # error) has computed only num_computed_tokens of its prompt.
+        num_tokens_after_batch = min(
+            req.num_computed_tokens,
+            max(req.num_prompt_tokens, req.num_tokens - 1),
+        )
+    else:
+        num_scheduled_tokens = scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens[req.request_id]
+        num_tokens_after_batch = req.num_computed_tokens + num_scheduled_tokens
+
+    num_offloadable_tokens = req_status.num_offloadable_tokens(num_tokens_after_batch)
+    prompt_offloadable_tokens = req_status.num_offloadable_tokens(req.num_prompt_tokens)
+
+    # Filter out chunks skipped due to sliding window attention / SSM
+    # or unreachable by the load path's alignment constraints.
+    new_offload_keys: list[OffloadKey] = []
+    group_store_ranges: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
+
+    apply_eagle_drop = not config.num_hash_lookahead_tokens
+    reachable_boundaries: tuple[int, ...] = ()
+    if config.retention_interval is not None:
+        reachable_boundaries = (req.num_prompt_tokens - 1,)
+        if req.shared_prefix_boundary:
+            reachable_boundaries += (req.shared_prefix_boundary,)
+
+    for group_config, group_state, stored_chunk_idx in zip(
+        config.kv_group_configs, req_status.group_states, start_chunk_idxs
+    ):
+        num_chunks = req_status.storable_chunks(
+            group_config, group_state, num_offloadable_tokens, apply_eagle_drop
+        )
+
+        start_chunk_idx = stored_chunk_idx
+        prompt_horizon_chunks = (
+            prompt_offloadable_tokens // group_config.tokens_per_chunk
+        )
+        final_swa_alignment_blocks = _final_swa_alignment_blocks(config, group_config)
+        reconsider_final_swa_tail = (
+            req.is_finished()
+            and num_chunks != prompt_horizon_chunks
+            and config.retention_interval is None
+            and final_swa_alignment_blocks is not None
+        )
+        if config.retention_interval is not None or group_config.is_eagle_group:
+            store_horizon_chunks = None
+        elif req.is_finished():
+            store_horizon_chunks = num_chunks
+        elif num_chunks <= prompt_horizon_chunks:
+            store_horizon_chunks = prompt_horizon_chunks
+        else:
+            # An active decode frontier is not a final request
+            # boundary. Only fixed alignment tails are reachable.
+            store_horizon_chunks = None
+        if reconsider_final_swa_tail:
+            assert final_swa_alignment_blocks is not None
+            horizon_blocks = num_chunks * blocks_per_chunk
+            partial_segment_start_block = (
+                horizon_blocks - horizon_blocks % final_swa_alignment_blocks
+            )
+            partial_segment_start_chunk = (
+                partial_segment_start_block // blocks_per_chunk
+            )
+            start_chunk_idx = min(start_chunk_idx, partial_segment_start_chunk)
+        group_store_ranges.append((start_chunk_idx, num_chunks))
+
+        if group_config.requires_cow_source:
+            continue
+
+        if num_chunks <= start_chunk_idx:
+            continue
+        offload_keys = group_state.offload_keys[start_chunk_idx:num_chunks]
+        # For each chunk, take the last corresponding GPU block. For
+        # blocks_per_chunk=3 and GPU block IDs 1 5 6 7 2 4 9 3 8,
+        # this selects GPU blocks 6 4 8.
+        # A block_id of 0 means either a sliding window / SSM skip
+        # or a stale entry that was zeroed out — skip it either way.
+        offload_block_ids = group_state.block_ids[
+            start_chunk_idx * blocks_per_chunk + blocks_per_chunk - 1 : num_chunks
+            * blocks_per_chunk : blocks_per_chunk
+        ]
+        assert len(offload_keys) == len(offload_block_ids)
+
+        # Use reachable_block_mask to filter unreachable chunks
+        # (SWA/Mamba sparsity + retention interval).
+        # reachable_block_mask operates in KV-block coordinates,
+        # so convert chunk indices to block indices.
+        block_mask = _reachable_store_block_mask(
+            config=config,
+            group_config=group_config,
+            start_chunk_idx=start_chunk_idx,
+            end_chunk_idx=num_chunks,
+            final_segment_end_chunk_idx=store_horizon_chunks,
+            reachable_boundaries=reachable_boundaries,
+        )
+
+        prompt_horizon_block_mask: list[bool] | None = None
+        if reconsider_final_swa_tail:
+            prompt_horizon_block_mask = _reachable_store_block_mask(
+                config=config,
+                group_config=group_config,
+                start_chunk_idx=start_chunk_idx,
+                end_chunk_idx=num_chunks,
+                final_segment_end_chunk_idx=prompt_horizon_chunks,
+                reachable_boundaries=reachable_boundaries,
+            )
+
+        for key_idx, (offload_key, block_id) in enumerate(
+            zip(offload_keys, offload_block_ids)
+        ):
+            if block_id == 0:
+                continue
+            abs_chunk_idx = start_chunk_idx + key_idx
+            if (
+                reconsider_final_swa_tail
+                and abs_chunk_idx < stored_chunk_idx
+                and (
+                    prompt_horizon_block_mask is None
+                    or any(
+                        prompt_horizon_block_mask[
+                            key_idx * blocks_per_chunk + block_idx
+                        ]
+                        for block_idx in range(blocks_per_chunk)
+                    )
+                )
+            ):
+                continue
+            # A chunk is reachable if any of its constituent
+            # blocks is reachable.
+            if block_mask is not None and not any(
+                block_mask[key_idx * blocks_per_chunk + b]
+                for b in range(blocks_per_chunk)
+            ):
+                continue
+            # A reachable null block would leave part of the chunk unwritten.
+            chunk_start = abs_chunk_idx * blocks_per_chunk
+            if any(
+                group_state.block_ids[chunk_start + b] == 0
+                and (block_mask is None or block_mask[key_idx * blocks_per_chunk + b])
+                for b in range(blocks_per_chunk)
+            ):
+                continue
+            new_offload_keys.append(offload_key)
+
+    return StoreCandidates(num_offloadable_tokens, new_offload_keys, group_store_ranges)
+
+
+def _reachable_store_block_mask(
+    config: SchedulerOffloadConfig,
+    group_config: GroupOffloadConfig,
+    start_chunk_idx: int,
+    end_chunk_idx: int,
+    final_segment_end_chunk_idx: int | None,
+    reachable_boundaries: tuple[int, ...],
+) -> list[bool] | None:
+    """Build the block mask for a range of candidate offload chunks."""
+    blocks_per_chunk = config.blocks_per_chunk
+    kv_cache_spec = group_config.kv_cache_spec
+    if isinstance(kv_cache_spec, SlidingWindowSpec) and (
+        kv_cache_spec.extra_retained_tokens
+    ):
+        # Offload restores all allocated history, including MTP re-prefill
+        # tokens. Widen only the store mask, not the model's attention window.
+        kv_cache_spec = replace(
+            kv_cache_spec,
+            sliding_window=(
+                kv_cache_spec.sliding_window + kv_cache_spec.extra_retained_tokens
+            ),
+            extra_retained_tokens=0,
+        )
+    return group_config.manager_cls.reachable_block_mask(
+        start_block=start_chunk_idx * blocks_per_chunk,
+        end_block=end_chunk_idx * blocks_per_chunk,
+        alignment_tokens=config.alignment_tokens,
+        kv_cache_spec=kv_cache_spec,
+        use_eagle=group_config.is_eagle_group,
+        retention_interval=config.retention_interval,
+        reachable_boundaries=reachable_boundaries,
+        dcp_world_size=config.dcp_world_size,
+        final_segment_end_block=(
+            final_segment_end_chunk_idx * blocks_per_chunk
+            if final_segment_end_chunk_idx is not None
+            else None
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def _final_swa_alignment_blocks(
+    config: SchedulerOffloadConfig, group_config: GroupOffloadConfig
+) -> int | None:
+    """Return representable final-tail alignment for a non-EAGLE SWA group."""
+    alignment_tokens = config.alignment_tokens
+    if (
+        alignment_tokens is None
+        or group_config.is_eagle_group
+        or not isinstance(group_config.kv_cache_spec, SlidingWindowSpec)
+        or alignment_tokens % group_config.tokens_per_block != 0
+    ):
+        return None
+    return alignment_tokens // group_config.tokens_per_block

+class OnComputeStoreHandler(StoreTriggerHandler):
+    """Offers each chunk when its KV data is computed (StoreTrigger.ON_COMPUTE)."""
+
+    trigger = StoreTrigger.ON_COMPUTE
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: SchedulerOffloadConfig,
+        events_tracker: OffloadingEventsTracker,
+    ):
+        super().__init__(config, events_tracker)
+        # req_id -> per group, the index of the next chunk to offer.
+        self._next_stored_chunk_idxs: dict[ReqId, list[int]] = {}
+
+    @override
+    def on_load_scheduled(
+        self,
+        req_status: RequestOffloadState,
+        num_cached_tokens: int,
+    ) -> None:
+        # Skip prefix-hit chunks for block-level policy; for
+        # request-level, the next stored chunk stays at 0 so all
+        # chunks (including hits) are offloaded.
+        if req_status.offloading_context.policy != OffloadPolicy.CHUNK_LEVEL:
+            return
+        self._next_stored_chunk_idxs[req_status.req.request_id] = [
+            cdiv(num_cached_tokens, group_config.tokens_per_chunk)
+            for group_config in self._config.kv_group_configs
+        ]
+
+    @override
+    def on_request_removed(self, req_id: ReqId) -> None:
+        self._next_stored_chunk_idxs.pop(req_id, None)
+
+    @override
+    def on_request_restarted(self, req_id: ReqId) -> None:
+        # Offer every chunk again.
+        self._next_stored_chunk_idxs.pop(req_id, None)
+
+    @override
+    def reset(self) -> None:
+        # Active requests store again from chunk 0.
+        self._next_stored_chunk_idxs.clear()
+
+    @override
+    def first_live_chunk_idx(
+        self, req_status: RequestOffloadState, config_idx: int
+    ) -> int | None:
+        next_idxs = self._next_stored_chunk_idxs.get(req_status.req.request_id)
+        return 0 if next_idxs is None else next_idxs[config_idx]
+
+    def _next_idxs(self, req_status: RequestOffloadState) -> list[int]:
+        """The next chunk to offer in each group, created at 0."""
+        req_id = req_status.req.request_id
+        next_idxs = self._next_stored_chunk_idxs.get(req_id)
+        if next_idxs is None:
+            next_idxs = [0] * len(req_status.group_states)
+            self._next_stored_chunk_idxs[req_id] = next_idxs
+        return next_idxs
+
+    def _advance_stored_idx(
+        self, req_status: RequestOffloadState, num_offloadable_tokens: int
+    ) -> None:
+        # max(): at the prefill->decode transition of a chunk-aligned prompt,
+        # storable_chunks drops by one (the eagle exclusion kicks in), and the
+        # index must not move backwards past already-stored chunks.
+        apply_eagle_drop = not self._config.num_hash_lookahead_tokens
+        next_idxs = self._next_idxs(req_status)
+        for config_idx, (group_config, group_state) in enumerate(
+            zip(self._config.kv_group_configs, req_status.group_states)
+        ):
+            next_idxs[config_idx] = max(
+                next_idxs[config_idx],
+                req_status.storable_chunks(
+                    group_config,
+                    group_state,
+                    num_offloadable_tokens,
+                    apply_eagle_drop,
+                ),
+            )
+

+    def build_store_jobs(
+        self,
+        scheduler_output: SchedulerOutput,
+        req_states: Mapping[ReqId, RequestOffloadState],
+        sink: StoreJobSink,
+    ) -> None:
+        blocks_per_chunk = self._config.blocks_per_chunk

+            scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens,
+            scheduler_output.finished_req_ids or (),

+            req_status = req_states.get(req_id)
+            if req_status is None:
+                continue
+            req = req_status.req
+            candidates = select_store_candidates(

+                scheduler_output,
+                req_status,
+                self._next_idxs(req_status),

+            num_offloadable_tokens = candidates.num_offloadable_tokens
+            new_offload_keys = candidates.keys
+            group_store_ranges = candidates.group_ranges
+
+            if not new_offload_keys:
+                self._advance_stored_idx(req_status, num_offloadable_tokens)
+                continue
+
+            store_output = sink.prepare_store(new_offload_keys, req_status.req_context)
+            if store_output is None:
+                logger.warning("Request %s: cannot store chunks", req_id)
+                continue
+
+            if not store_output.keys_to_store:
+                self._advance_stored_idx(req_status, num_offloadable_tokens)
+                continue
+
+            ordered_keys_to_store = tuple(dict.fromkeys(store_output.keys_to_store))
+            keys_to_store = set(ordered_keys_to_store)
+
+            group_sizes: list[int] = []
+            block_indices: list[int] = []
+            src_block_ids: list[int] = []
+            fenced_block_ids: list[int] = []
+            deferred_fence_block_ids: list[int] = []
+            for group_config, group_state, store_range in zip(
+                self._config.kv_group_configs,
+                req_status.group_states,
+                group_store_ranges,
+            ):
+                is_sliding_window = (
+                    group_config.sliding_window_size_in_chunks is not None
+                )
+                start_chunk_idx, num_chunks = store_range
+                block_ids = group_state.block_ids
+                num_group_blocks = 0
+                start_gpu_block_idx: int | None = None
+                for idx, offload_key in enumerate(
+                    group_state.offload_keys[start_chunk_idx:num_chunks]
+                ):
+                    if offload_key not in keys_to_store:
+                        continue
+
+                    chunk_idx = start_chunk_idx + idx
+
+                    self._events_tracker.record_store(
+                        req, group_config, chunk_idx, offload_key
+                    )
+
+                    gpu_block_idx = chunk_idx * blocks_per_chunk
+                    if start_gpu_block_idx is None:
+                        start_gpu_block_idx = gpu_block_idx
+                    for i in range(blocks_per_chunk):
+                        block_id = block_ids[gpu_block_idx + i]
+                        # Keep null pages inside the chunk as placeholders so
+                        # later blocks retain their logical offsets in the CPU
+                        # chunk. The null GPU block is zeroed and can be copied
+                        # safely; it must not be fenced as a live allocation.
+                        src_block_ids.append(block_id)
+                        num_group_blocks += 1

+                            continue
+                        if is_sliding_window:
+                            fenced_block_ids.append(block_id)

+                            deferred_fence_block_ids.append(block_id)

+                group_sizes.append(num_group_blocks)
+                block_indices.append(start_gpu_block_idx or 0)
+
+            next_idxs = self._next_idxs(req_status)
+            for config_idx, (_, num_chunks) in enumerate(group_store_ranges):
+                next_idxs[config_idx] = max(next_idxs[config_idx], num_chunks)
+
+            # the non-sliding window blocks will be watched only
+            # when the request finishes
+            sink.add_job(
+                req_id,
+                ordered_keys_to_store,
+                GPULoadStoreSpec(
+                    src_block_ids,
+                    group_sizes=group_sizes,
+                    block_indices=block_indices,
+                ),
+                store_output.store_spec,
+                fenced_block_ids=fenced_block_ids or None,
+                deferred_fence_block_ids=deferred_fence_block_ids,
+            )

+class OnHandoffStoreHandler(StoreTriggerHandler):
+    """Stores the state blocks that the KV cache manager hands off
+    (StoreTrigger.ON_HANDOFF).
+
+    The hand-off arrives when a recurrent state block is about to be reused.
+    Its source is short-lived, so every store mode stores it at the same step.
+    """
+
+    trigger = StoreTrigger.ON_HANDOFF
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: SchedulerOffloadConfig,
+        events_tracker: OffloadingEventsTracker,
+    ):
+        super().__init__(config, events_tracker)
+        self._cow_source_groups = frozenset(
+            group_config.group_idx
+            for group_config in config.kv_group_configs
+            if group_config.requires_cow_source
+        )
+
+    @override
+    def first_live_chunk_idx(
+        self, req_status: RequestOffloadState, config_idx: int
+    ) -> int | None:
+        # The source blocks come from the scheduler output, not from the
+        # request's block list.
+        return None
+
+    @override
+    def build_store_jobs(
+        self,
+        scheduler_output: SchedulerOutput,
+        req_states: Mapping[ReqId, RequestOffloadState],
+        sink: StoreJobSink,
+    ) -> None:
+        block_state = scheduler_output.kv_connector_block_state
+        handoffs = block_state.boundary_state_offloads if block_state else None
+        if not handoffs:
+            return
+        self._build_aligned_boundary_store_jobs(handoffs, req_states, sink)
+        if self._config.supports_partial_tail:
+            self._build_partial_tail_store_jobs(
+                scheduler_output, handoffs, req_states, sink
+            )
+
+    def _build_aligned_boundary_store_jobs(
+        self,
+        handoffs: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, int]]],
+        req_states: Mapping[ReqId, RequestOffloadState],
+        sink: StoreJobSink,
+    ) -> None:
+        num_groups = len(self._config.kv_group_configs)
+        config_idx_by_group = {
+            config.group_idx: idx
+            for idx, config in enumerate(self._config.kv_group_configs)
+        }
+        for req_id, entries in handoffs.items():
+            req_status = req_states.get(req_id)
+            if req_status is None:
+                continue
+            req = req_status.req
+            max_boundary = req_status.num_offloadable_tokens(req.num_tokens)
+            for group_idx, block_id, boundary in entries:
+                config_idx = config_idx_by_group.get(group_idx)
+                if config_idx is None:
+                    continue
+                group_config = self._config.kv_group_configs[config_idx]
+                if (
+                    block_id == 0
+                    or boundary > max_boundary
+                    or boundary % group_config.tokens_per_chunk != 0
+                ):
+                    continue

+                key = req_status.register_boundary_key(group_idx, boundary)
+                store_output = sink.prepare_store([key], req_status.req_context)
+                if store_output is None:
+                    continue
+                if not store_output.keys_to_store:
+                    continue
+
+                group_sizes = [0] * num_groups
+                group_sizes[config_idx] = 1
+                block_indices = [0] * num_groups
+                block_indices[config_idx] = (
+                    boundary // group_config.tokens_per_block - 1
+                )
+                sink.add_job(

+                    [key],

+                        block_indices=block_indices,

+                    store_output.store_spec,
+                    fenced_block_ids=[block_id],

+                    req,
+                    group_config,
+                    boundary // group_config.tokens_per_chunk - 1,
+                    key,
+                )

+    def _build_partial_tail_store_jobs(

+        scheduler_output: SchedulerOutput,

+        req_states: Mapping[ReqId, RequestOffloadState],
+        sink: StoreJobSink,
+    ) -> None:
+        partial_tail_block_size = self._config.partial_tail_block_size
+        max_eagle_proof_margin = self._config.max_eagle_proof_margin

+            entries = [
+                entry for entry in entries if entry[2] % partial_tail_block_size != 0

+                continue

+                continue

+            boundary = boundaries.pop()
+            req = req_status.req
+            group_states = {

+                for group, state in zip(
+                    self._config.kv_group_configs, req_status.group_states
+                )
+            }
+            max_boundary = min(
+                req.num_prompt_tokens,
+                req_status.max_offload_tokens or req.num_prompt_tokens,
+            )
+            assert boundary > 0
+            assert boundary % self._config.tokens_per_hash == 0
+            assert boundary <= max_boundary

+            if max_eagle_proof_margin:
+                # The CoW hand-off arrives on the step that computes the prompt

+                # forward, so count the prompt tokens this step computes.
+                prompt_tokens_after_step = min(
+                    req.num_computed_tokens

+                    req.num_prompt_tokens,

+                if boundary + max_eagle_proof_margin > prompt_tokens_after_step:
+                    # The EAGLE proof is not computed by the end of this step.
+                    continue

+            cow_blocks = {group_idx: block_id for group_idx, block_id, _ in entries}
+            assert self._cow_source_groups.issubset(cow_blocks)

+            if any(

+                and block_idx >= len(group_states[group.group_idx].block_ids)
+                for group in self._config.kv_group_configs
+            ):
+                continue
+            key_tokens = [
+                self._config.partial_tail_key_tokens(config_idx, boundary)
+                for config_idx in range(len(self._config.kv_group_configs))
+            ]
+            keys = [
+                req_status.register_boundary_key(group.group_idx, tokens)
+                for group, tokens in zip(self._config.kv_group_configs, key_tokens)
+            ]
+            block_ids = [
+                cow_blocks[group.group_idx]
+                if group.group_idx in self._cow_source_groups
+                else group_states[group.group_idx].block_ids[block_idx]
+                for group in self._config.kv_group_configs
+            ]
+            assert all(block_id != 0 for block_id in block_ids)
+
+            store_output = sink.prepare_store(keys, req_status.req_context)
+            if store_output is None:
+                continue
+            if not store_output.keys_to_store:
+                continue
+
+            for group_config, tokens, key in zip(
+                self._config.kv_group_configs, key_tokens, keys
+            ):
+                if key in store_output.keys_to_store:
+                    self._events_tracker.record_partial_store(
+                        req, group_config, tokens, key
+                    )
+
+            group_by_key = {key: idx for idx, key in enumerate(keys)}
+            accepted_groups = [group_by_key[key] for key in store_output.keys_to_store]
+            group_sizes = [0] * len(self._config.kv_group_configs)
+            block_indices = [0] * len(self._config.kv_group_configs)
+            for group_idx in accepted_groups:
+                group_sizes[group_idx] = 1
+                block_indices[group_idx] = block_idx
+            source_blocks = [block_ids[group_idx] for group_idx in accepted_groups]
+
+            sink.add_job(
+                req_id,
+                store_output.keys_to_store,
+                GPULoadStoreSpec(
+                    source_blocks,
+                    group_sizes=group_sizes,
+                    block_indices=block_indices,
+                ),
+                store_output.store_spec,
+                fenced_block_ids=source_blocks,
+            )

inline_comments.body:
This will be useful for lazy offloading as well.
Claude suggests we put them in their own handler:

**Where should the hand-off stores live?**

`OnComputeStoreHandler` holds two store kinds that are not `ON_COMPUTE` stores: the aligned boundary stores and the partial-tail CoW stores, both fed by `kv_connector_block_state.boundary_state_offloads`. They differ from chunk stores in three ways:

- **Who decides when.** The KV cache manager sends the hand-off when the recurrent state block is about to be reused. Neither the eager nor the lazy policy picks that moment.
- **The source is short-lived.** The CoW copy is offered once, so the store can't be postponed. Lazy mode must store it at the same step as eager mode.
- **No per-request progress.** It never reads `_next_stored_chunk_idxs`; it works from `req_status` and the hand-off only.

So every store mode stores these the same way, at the same time. That makes it a trigger of its own, not part of `ON_COMPUTE`. If it stays in `OnComputeStoreHandler`, a manager that later selects only `ON_OVERWRITE` or lazy silently stops storing Mamba `align` state. Hybrid models then get no prefix hits from offload, and nothing in the logs says why.

Suggested layout:

```
store_triggers/
  base.py        StoreTriggerHandler
  on_compute.py  OnComputeStoreHandler   (chunk stores only)
  handoff.py     HandoffStoreHandler     (aligned boundary + partial tail, _cow_source_groups)
  candidates.py  select_store_candidates (was common.py; avoids two `common` modules)
```

- Add `StoreTrigger.ON_HANDOFF`, so the manager sees the real cause. A lazy manager can then admit these stores without running its overwrite admission.
- The scheduler adds this handler on its own whenever the config can produce hand-offs (`supports_partial_tail` or any `requires_cow_source` group). The manager doesn't select it. A manager can still decline these stores in `prepare_store`.
- Run it before `OnComputeStoreHandler`. That keeps today's job-ID order, so this stays a pure move.
- It also retires the name `_build_partial_tail_store_jobs`, which today also runs the aligned-boundary path.

+    """Offers each chunk when its KV data is computed (StoreTrigger.ON_COMPUTE)."""

+        partial = self._build_partial_tail_store_jobs(scheduler_output, req_states)

+        self,
+        handoffs: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, int]]],
+        req_states: Mapping[ReqId, RequestOffloadState],

+        output = StoreJobsOutput()
+        num_groups = len(self._config.kv_group_configs)
+        config_idx_by_group = {

+            req_status = req_states.get(req_id)
+            if req_status is None:
+                continue
+            req = req_status.req
+            max_boundary = req_status.num_offloadable_tokens(req.num_tokens)
+            for group_idx, block_id, boundary in entries:
+                config_idx = config_idx_by_group.get(group_idx)
+                if config_idx is None:
+                    continue
+                group_config = self._config.kv_group_configs[config_idx]
+                if (
+                    block_id == 0
+                    or boundary > max_boundary
+                    or boundary % group_config.tokens_per_chunk != 0
+                ):
+                    continue
+
+                key = req_status.register_boundary_key(group_idx, boundary)
+                store_output = self._prepare_store([key], req_status.req_context)
+                if store_output is None:
+                    output.num_allocation_failures += 1
+                    continue
+                if not store_output.keys_to_store:
+                    continue

+                group_sizes = [0] * num_groups
+                group_sizes[config_idx] = 1

+                        GPULoadStoreSpec(

+                            block_indices=block_indices,

+                )

+                    group_config,
+                    boundary // group_config.tokens_per_chunk - 1,

+
+@dataclass
+class StoreJobsOutput:
+    """The store jobs of one handler in one scheduler step."""
+
+    # The scheduler gives each job its ID, in this order.
+    jobs: list[tuple[TransferJob, TransferJobStatus]] = field(default_factory=list)
+    # Number of prepare_store calls that returned None.
+    num_allocation_failures: int = 0
+
+
+class StoreTriggerHandler(ABC):
+    """Makes the store jobs of one StoreTrigger.
+
+    The handler offers chunks to the manager and describes the store jobs. The
+    scheduler gives the jobs their IDs, tracks them, and completes them.
+
+    Handlers are isolated. A handler does not know of other handlers, and its
+    result does not depend on which handlers run, or on their order. A handler
+    keeps its own state. The scheduler holds only global state, and gives the
+    same hooks to each handler.
+    """
+
+    # The trigger that this handler serves.
+    trigger: ClassVar[StoreTrigger]
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: SchedulerOffloadConfig,
+        manager: OffloadingManager,
+        events_tracker: OffloadingEventsTracker,
+    ):
+        self._config = config
+        # A handler offers chunks only through _prepare_store.
+        self._manager = manager
+        self._events_tracker = events_tracker
+
+    def _prepare_store(
+        self, keys: Collection[OffloadKey], req_context: ReqContext
+    ) -> PrepareStoreOutput | None:
+        """Offer keys to the manager, with the trigger of this handler."""
+        return self._manager.prepare_store(keys, req_context, self.trigger)
+
+    def _make_store_job(
+        self,
+        req_id: ReqId,
+        keys: Collection[OffloadKey],
+        src_spec: GPULoadStoreSpec,
+        dst_spec: LoadStoreSpec,
+        fenced_block_ids: list[int] | None = None,
+        deferred_fence_block_ids: list[int] | None = None,
+    ) -> tuple[TransferJob, TransferJobStatus]:
+        """Make a store job, and the status that tracks it.
+
+        Args:
+            req_id: the request that owns the blocks.
+            keys: the keys that the job stores.
+            src_spec: the GPU blocks to read.
+            dst_spec: where the manager stores the blocks.
+            fenced_block_ids: the source blocks to fence from job creation.
+            deferred_fence_block_ids: the source blocks to fence after the
+                request finishes.
+
+        """
+        job = TransferJob(req_id=req_id, src_spec=src_spec, dst_spec=dst_spec)
+        job_status = TransferJobStatus(
+            req_id=req_id,
+            pending_count=self._config.num_workers,
+            keys=set(keys),
+            is_store=True,
+            deferred_fence_block_ids=deferred_fence_block_ids,
+            fenced_block_ids=fenced_block_ids,
+            trigger=self.trigger,
